subject: VPC maintenance: staged failure-injection & rollback checklist
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.example.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.example.com, ops@acme.example.com
Cc: partners@cloudvendor.com
Date: 2027-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: VPC maintenance: staged failure-injection & rollback checklist

Team / ACME ops —

As discussed in yesterday's architecture review, we're proposing a staged failure-injection during the upcoming maintenance window to validate our rollback surfaces and version pin transitions for the Private (VPC) deployment. The goal is to surface any latent KV-cache migration issues and confirm our automated fallback paths (model variant fallback + routing policy) without impacting production traffic beyond the agreed blast radius.

High-level plan (attached: vpc_failure_injection_runbook.pdf):
- Window: Sep 14, 02:00–04:00 UTC (ACME requested local 19:00–21:00 PT on Sep 13; see schedule .ics)
- Stage A: Canary node cordon + controlled model reload (non-pinned variant) — verify metrics converge
- Stage B: KV cache invalidation on canary, then selective shard restart — observe latency/error trends
- Stage C: Induce degraded GPU perf on canary (cpu fallback path) to validate routing to lower-cost variant
- Rollback triggers: >2% sustained error delta over 10m, or p95 latency > 1.5x baseline for 5m
- Rollback path: pin to prior model version, re-route traffic to Dedicated fallback pool, clear KV cache only as last resort

Action items for this thread:
1) Aditya: confirm that pinned-version manifest will be available and who will push it (CI or manual).
2) Kimberly: add our canary monitoring dashboard links and define the alert thresholds in the runbook.
3) ACME ops: confirm you can allow the specified window and that your on-call will be available to confirm network path changes.
4) Dylan: run the failure-injection rehearsal in staging next week and post the logs to the drive folder above.

Attachments: vpc_failure_injection_runbook.pdf, rollback_playbook.md, maintenance_schedule.ics

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.example.com, ops@acme.example.com
Date: 2027-09-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC maintenance: staged failure-injection & rollback checklist

Grace —

Thanks for the clear plan. A couple of technical clarifications from the runtime side:

- Version pinning: We will produce a pinned-manifest tag as a static artifact (s3://redwood-pinned-manifests/acme/2027-09-13.json). CI will *not* push it automatically for safety; this should be a manual jump performed by infra on the scheduled run. I can own generation and validation of the manifest.

- Kernel/quantization caveat: when we trigger the degraded GPU perf (Stage C), older model variants on the fallback pool use a different quantization profile — we should add an explicit regression check for token-level coherence (short prompt set) so we can detect quality regressions that are not visible via latency metrics. Suggestion: add a small eval set in rollback_playbook.md that runs at each failover step.

- Observability: I'll add trace tags to mark failure-injection traffic so we can filter it out from production analytics.

I'll attach a short script snippet (in the drive runbook) to validate the pinned-manifest checksum before applying.

Aditya
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: VPC maintenance: staged failure-injection & rollback checklist

Harish / team —

We can accept the later window (Sep 13, 21:00–23:00 PT). Clarifications below: 

- Routing: Redwood will perform in-band model routing; ACME does not need to change route tables for the planned stages. If we hit a network-level failure (unlikely in the controlled canary), we'll coordinate for a manual cutover.
- Staging rehearsal ETA: Dylan and I will run the staging rehearsal next Tue (Sep 12). I'll add the monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds to the runbook (see rollback_playbook.md). Key alerts we'll add: request-error-rate, p95 latency delta, token-coherence regression (small prompt eval), and sagemaker/gpu-oom signals.
- On-call contact: infra lead is Aditya Rao (cell: +1-415-555-0147). Please confirm you've got that recorded.

Quick checklist summary (included in rollback_playbook.md):
1) Pre-window validation: manifest checksum, canary health baseline snapshot, alert mute rules for expected noise.
2) Execution: staged canary steps A→B→C with 15m observation windows.
3) Rollback: apply pinned-manifest + cache-warmup on fallback pool + re-route traffic; expect 8–12m to stabilize.
4) Post-run: run short eval set and produce a short incident note with metric deltas.

I'll upload the updated playbook this afternoon.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

All —

I ran the rehearsal in staging today (logs uploaded to the drive link). No blocking regressions found after two iterations, but note the token-coherence test flagged a subtle drop on one prompt for the quantized fallback variant; added a mitigation note to rollback_playbook.md (we'll increase sampling during the live run).

We're good to proceed with the shifted window. Confirming: Sep 13, 21:00–23:00 PT, Aditya on-call, Kimberly monitoring, Grace coordinating with ACME.

Dylan
Senior DevOps Engineer, Redwood Inference
